title: SELF-DEFENDED, AUTONOMOUSLY SECURE SPACECRAFTS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop and implement a proof of concept of a self-defended, autonomously secure spacecraft.Description: ESA Vision is to move towards highly autonomous systems in order to revolutionize space missions. To achieve this, there is a need to automate also the security functions and self-defense of the spacecraft itself. In addition to an activity on Intelligent Space Systems, thisactivity is complementary by filling the gap on security aspects. The very large number of satellites, the dense and complicated geopolitical environment, as well as the concept of highly autonomous systems themselves make it necessary to also invest on the self-defense of the satellites themselves. To implement autonomous space missions, spacecrafts must automate all the security functions, e.g. key management, that allows them to operate securely without intervention from ground segment operators. In addition, spacecrafts need to maintain a Space Situational Awareness (SSA), which involves the comprehensive monitoring, tracking, and analysis of objects and activities in space, including potential malicious ones. The information collected through on-board sensors must me automatically tracked, analysed, identified, correlated and categorised on board, enabling detection, prediction, warning and triggering of automated reaction for mitigation or secure spacecraft restoration when needed. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Perform a state-off-the-art on space intelligent platforms and on spacecraft autonomous systems - Based on space security reference architecture, and threat analysis, identify security services to be automated and technologies that need to be developed to implement aself-defense spacecraft - Design an architecture for autonomously secure, self defense spacecrafts - Develop a proof-of-concept in a simulated environment, where basic spacecraft security functions are automated, information from (simulated or emulated) sensors is collected, analysed, correlated, and categorised, while security measures implemented on board are triggered, incl. automatically reconfiguration to restore secure operations. - Test the proof-of-concept based on pre-defined scenarios - Identify gaps and proposeroadmap for further evolution Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.

title: FORUM DATA INNOVATION AND SCIENCE CLUSTER DISC
description: FORUM, ESA's 9th Earth Explorer mission, is currently planned for launch in Q4 2028, with a nominal mission lifetime of five years.The mission will provide interferometric measurements across the 6.25-100 m spectral range, including the Far Infrared (FIR, approximately 15-100 m), which accounts for approximately 50% of the Earth's outgoing longwave radiation and up to 60% in polar regions.By addressing this critical observational gap, FORUM will provide unique measurements to advance our understanding of the Earth's energy budget and enable detailed investigations of the role and interactions of essential climate variables.The purpose of this procurement is to establish the FORUM Data Innovation and Science Cluster (DISC). The DISC concept has been successfully implemented byESA for previous Earth Explorer missions and is based on a consortium bringing together the scientific and technical expertise required to support the specific objectives and data quality needs of the mission.The FORUM DISC consortium will support ESA's Earth Observation Programmes - Sensor Performance, Products and Algorithms Section (EOP-GMQ) in the generation, calibration and validation (Cal/Val), monitoring, and quality control (QC) of FORUM mission products, as well as in their maintenance and evolution throughout the mission lifetime.The FORUM DISC contract will be structured into three main phases:Pre-launch phase: covering primarily the development, integration, verification and preparation for operational use of the FORUM processors, together with the associated quality monitoring and calibration/validation tools and procedures.Commissioning phase: covering the in-orbit commissioning activities, including the operation and validation of the implemented processors, tools and procedures, as well as the initial calibration and validation of FORUM mission products.Operations and mission exploitation phase: covering the nominal Cal/Val and quality monitoring activities during Phase E2 of the mission, together with the maintenance and evolution of algorithms, products, and processors.

checks.text: The DISC concept has been successfully implemented byESA for previous Earth Explorer missions and is based on a consortium bringing together the scientific and technical expertise required to support the specific objectives and data quality needs of the mission.

The FORUM DISC consortium will support ESA's Earth Observation Programmes - Sensor Performance, Products and Algorithms Section (EOP-GMQ) in the generation, calibration and validation (Cal/Val), monitoring, and quality control (QC) of FORUM mission products, as well as in their maintenance and evolution throughout the mission lifetime.
